originales.texto:
[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 2. Four schools worth stealing] **Race-truth (Frankenheimer, Lelouch, Mangold/Papamichael, Howard/Dod Mantle, Refn).** Speed is a fact you earn by putting the camera where a real rig could bolt — bumper, hood lip, hostess-tray, axle, cabin. Low, wide and close, hard-mounted without vibration isolation so "cheeks shake", asphalt streaking in frame as the speedometer, mini-cams next to pistons and swelling tires for "an electron-microscope view of the car at its limit". Refn's cocoon: silence and stillness inside the shell, chaos outside, so the launch detonates. Refuse the crank — *Grand Prix* oiled tires for real smoke rather than fake the burnout.
→ **Rule:** if the implied camera could not physically mount on the car, the panel reads as render — drop it to bumper height and bolt it on.

originales.texto: [Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.] Every shot owns three concrete physical details: one environmental pressure, one physical micro-action, one sound or visual motif anchor.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.

originales.texto:
[Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.] Every shot in every prompt owns at least three concrete physical details:
1. **One environmental pressure.** Cold blue refrigerator light. Steam off boiling water. Wet asphalt. Flickering fluorescent. Dripping tap. Curtain breathing in the AC. (Kurosawa: weather is a character. See `dramaturgy.md` §9.)
2. **One physical micro-action.** Jaw locks. Knuckles whiten on the fork. Lips press into a line. He swallows hard. Fingers curl against the doorframe. (Show, not tell — the body is the only place where feelings render.)
3. **One sound anchor or visual motif.** Stomach growl at 2.3s. Reflection in a darkened phone screen. Rain on the same windowpane. A single fluorescent flicker before each cut.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.

originales.texto:
[Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt. › The three-detail rule] For each shot in the storyboard or prompt, before it is sent, the writer commits to:
1. **Environmental pressure.** A physical fact about the space that carries the emotion. Cold refrigerator light. Wet asphalt. Flickering ceiling tube. Steam from the kettle. Rain on one specific windowpane. A buzzing AC unit. Tight corridor walls. Mirror reflection. (See §9 — Environment plays.)
2. **Physical micro-action on the body.** The emotion translated into the actor's body. Jaw locks. Knuckles whiten. Lips press flat. Eyes drop a quarter-inch. He swallows hard. Fingers curl against the doorframe. The actor's body is the only place where feelings render — names of feelings do not.
3. **Sound anchor or visual motif.** A recurring perceptual hook tied to the spine of the piece. Stomach growl repeated three times. Reflection in dark glass on every transition. The same musical sting at every Crack beat. The clock's second hand. Footsteps in an empty corridor.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt. › The three-detail rule

originales.texto:
[Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)] Before returning the final prompt to the user, audit every shot. Each shot must carry at least one of each:
1. Environmental pressure (lighting, weather, surface, sound of the room).
2. Physical micro-action on the body (jaw, hand, breath, eye, gesture).
3. Sound anchor or recurring visual motif tied to the emotional spine.

grupos.fusionado: Regla de los tres detalles (lo no negociable de las reglas universales de video y segunda ley de dramaturgia "Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt."): cada shot de cada prompt o storyboard carga al menos tres detalles físicos concretos, y el escritor se compromete a ellos antes de enviarlo: 1. Una presión ambiental: un hecho físico del espacio que carga la emoción (iluminación, clima, superficie, sonido de la habitación); ejemplos: cold blue refrigerator light, steam off boiling water / from the kettle, wet asphalt, flickering fluorescent / ceiling tube, dripping tap, curtain breathing in the AC, rain on one specific windowpane, a buzzing AC unit, tight corridor walls, mirror reflection (Kurosawa: el clima es un personaje; ver `dramaturgy.md` §9 — Environment plays). 2. Una micro-acción física en el cuerpo: la emoción traducida al cuerpo del actor (mandíbula, mano, respiración, ojo, gesto); ejemplos: jaw locks, knuckles whiten (on the fork), lips press into a line / flat, eyes drop a quarter-inch, he swallows hard, fingers curl against the doorframe; el cuerpo del actor es el único lugar donde los sentimientos se renderizan, los nombres de sentimientos no (show, not tell). 3. Un ancla sonora o motivo visual: un gancho perceptivo recurrente atado a la columna emocional de la pieza; ejemplos: stomach growl at 2.3s / repetido tres veces, reflection in a darkened phone screen / in dark glass on every transition, rain on the same windowpane, a single fluorescent flicker before each cut, the same musical sting at every Crack beat, the clock's second hand, footsteps in an empty corridor. U12 (The three-detail check, audit before sending): antes de devolver el prompt final al usuario, auditar cada shot; cada uno debe llevar al menos uno de cada. En el chequeo de dramaturgia antes de enviar cualquier prompt, pregunta 2: ¿pasa cada shot el three-detail check (presión ambiental + micro-acción física + motivo sonoro o visual)?

originales.texto:
[Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)] Seedance does not render abstractions. It renders **physical specifics**. Every adjective must be a sensory fact. Every emotion must be a body. Every shot must own at least three concrete details:
1. **One environmental pressure.** Cold blue refrigerator light. Steam off boiling water. Wet asphalt. Flickering fluorescent. Dripping tap. Curtain breathing in the AC.
2. **One physical micro-action.** Jaw locks. Finger taps the counter. Knuckles whiten on the fork. Lips press into a line. He swallows hard.
3. **One sound anchor or visual motif.** Stomach growl at 2.3s. Reflection in the dark phone screen. Rain hitting the same windowpane.

originales.texto: [Adapter: Seedance 2.0 (motion-aware video, multi-shot)] Seedance 2.0 is the multi-shot model. It can generate a **short sequence of cuts in a single generation** while holding subject and environment consistency across them. Reach for it when several consecutive storyboard beats share one subject and you want them to feel like one continuous take, it beats stitching four independent Kling clips that drift apart. For a single isolated shot, Kling is the simpler default.

Usar el modo multi-shot sequence cuando 2–4 beats consecutivos del storyboard comparten un sujeto y se quiere continuidad, que se sientan como una toma continua; supera a coser cuatro clips independientes de Kling que derivan. [Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits] What the format cannot guarantee is the judgement in between. Applying a `fix` field means
reading a sentence of English and editing prose, so hold yourself to the narrowest edit
that satisfies the fix and leave every other layer byte-identical. If you find yourself
rewriting a prompt the critique did not ask you to touch, stop: that is drift, and it will
read as a mystery six shots later.

grupos.fusionado: Revisión de delta mínimo (small-delta revision; Learning Registry v3.2 del AI Production Director, aprendizaje `lrn32_small_delta_revision`, efecto=REQUIRE, prioridad=915): al corregir un fallo localizado en un asset o prompt que por lo demás pasa, está aceptado o es fuerte, cambiar solo el/los elemento(s) fallido(s); no reescribir ni reinterpretar los locks no afectados. Motivo: las reescrituras verbosas repetidas degradaron la adherencia, mientras las ediciones locales preservaron las fortalezas. En el revision mode de visual-prompt-forge (Determinism, and its limits): lo que el formato no puede garantizar es el juicio intermedio; aplicar un campo `fix` implica leer una frase en inglés y editar prosa, así que hay que ceñirse a la edición más estrecha que satisfaga el fix y dejar cada otra capa byte-idéntica. Si te encuentras reescribiendo un prompt que la crítica no pidió tocar, para: eso es drift, y se leerá como un misterio seis shots después.
